digest.component_or_area: hardening test oracle and legacy output fixture
propositions: The hardening byte-equivalence oracle executes both production _convert and a copied _legacy_convert for 884 corpus units, with the legacy oracle sharing mutable _PANDOC_TO constant with production, causing both sides to mutate identically when format changes.
The immutable legacy-output fixture must replace the copied subprocess call while preserving all 884 real production _convert/Pandoc invocations in per-change CI to maintain the stated test contract.

The fixture schema must store exact Pandoc version and platform-specific binary SHA-256 fingerprints (darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64) and validate against the current platform, failing on version drift or hash mismatch.
Deterministic fixture regeneration and a fast installed-version/platform drift assertion must prevent silent conversion behavior drift across platforms and Pandoc versions.
The defect-seeded mutation (_PANDOC_TO=plain) must cause the independent byte-equivalence oracle to fail RED while production conversion continues to invoke real Pandoc.

Gerrit patchset 1 failed all Ubuntu cells because the schema emitted only macOS-arm64 SHA-256 and treated it as platform-independent; patchset 2 added platform-keyed fingerprint map and passed 7/7 jobs with 884 eliminated subprocesses.
